title: Stalk of internal Hom for a finitely presented module
statement: Let $(X,\mathcal O_X)$ be a ringed space, let $\mathcal F$ be a finitely presented $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module, and let $x\in X$. For the internal sheaf Hom $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], the canonical map $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)_x\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal F_x,\mathcal G_x)$, sending a germ of a local morphism to its induced stalk map, is an isomorphism.

source.place: Modules, Lemma Tag 01CP (lemma-stalk-internal-hom), lines 3619-3678: finitely presented case via a finite free presentation and exactness of internal Hom

proof.text: *Step 1 (the canonical map).* An element of $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)_x$ is a germ of a section over an open $U\ni x$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], i.e. of an $\mathcal O_U$-linear $\varphi:\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal G|_U$ [def-pur-sheaf-hom], [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Since the open neighbourhoods of $x$ inside $U$ are cofinal among all open neighbourhoods of $x$, $(\mathcal F|_U)_x=\mathcal F_x$ and $(\mathcal G|_U)_x=\mathcal G_x$ (same germs), so $\varphi$ has a stalk map $\varphi_x:\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal G_x$, $s_x\mapsto\varphi_W(s)_x$ for $s\in\mathcal F(W)$, $x\in W\subseteq U$, which is $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. If $\varphi|_V=\varphi'|_V$ on an open $x\in V\subseteq U\cap U'$ then $\varphi_x=\varphi'_x$ (compute on germs of sections over opens inside $V$). Hence $c:\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)_x\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal F_x,\mathcal G_x)$, $(U,\varphi)_x\mapsto\varphi_x$, is well defined; it is additive, and $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear because for $f\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ the section $f\varphi$ (multiplication by $f$ composed with $\varphi$, [def-pur-sheaf-hom]) has $(f\varphi)_x=f_x\varphi_x$ by the formula $(rs)_x=r_xs_x$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk].

source.place: proof, first paragraph: 'The map sends the equivalence class of (U, phi) ... to phi_x'

proof.text: *Step 2 (localize to a finite presentation).* By [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation](2) there are an open $U\ni x$, integers $n,m\ge0$, an $\mathcal O_U$-linear $a:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ and an isomorphism $\iota:\operatorname{Coker}(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F|_U$ in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_U)$; let $b=\iota\circ\pi:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$, $\pi$ the cokernel map, and write $a_U(e_k)=\sum_ia_{ik}e_i$ with $a_{ik}\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ (here $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ is $W\mapsto\mathcal O_X(W)^{\oplus n}$ with basis sections $e_i$). The sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal F|_U\to0$ is exact in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_U)$: by [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](3) applied on the ringed space $(U,\mathcal O_U)$, for every $y\in U$ the map $\pi_y$ is surjective with kernel $a_y(\mathcal O_{U,y}^{\oplus m})$, and $\iota_y$ is bijective (its inverse is $(\iota^{-1})_y$, stalk maps being functorial by their formula in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]); so $b_y$ is surjective with kernel $\operatorname{Im}a_y$, i.e. the complexes $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$ and $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U\to0$ are exact on every stalk, hence exact by [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](5). Finally, sections of $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)$ over opens $V\subseteq U$ are $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_V}(\mathcal F|_V,\mathcal G|_V)$, which are also the sections of $\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal F|_U,\mathcal G|_U)$ over $V$, with the same restriction maps and module structures [def-pur-sheaf-hom], [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]; with the cofinality of Step 1, the stalks at $x$, the stalks $\mathcal F_x,\mathcal G_x,\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and the map $c$ are unchanged when $X$ is replaced by $U$. We may and do assume $U=X$.

source.place: proof, third paragraph: 'By localizing on X we may assume that F has a presentation O^m -> O^n -> F -> 0'

proof.text: *Step 3 (the free case on the sheaf side).* By [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-hom-finite-presentation-kernel](2), applied to the exact sequence $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal F\to0$ of Step 2 and to $\mathcal M=\mathcal G$, the sequence $0\to\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)\xrightarrow{\beta}\mathcal G^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal G^{\oplus m}$, $\beta_V(\psi)=(\psi_V(b_V(e_i|_V)))_i$, $\alpha_V((y_i)_i)=(\sum_ia_{ik}|_Vy_i)_k$, is an exact sequence of $\mathcal O_X$-modules.

source.place: proof, third paragraph: 'By Lemma 01CO this gives an exact sequence 0 -> Hom(F,G) -> G^n -> G^m'

proof.text: *Step 4 (taking stalks).* By [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](5) (with (2): $\beta$ is a kernel of $\alpha$, so $\beta_x$ is injective with image $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_x$) the sequence $0\to\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)_x\xrightarrow{\beta_x}(\mathcal G^{\oplus n})_x\xrightarrow{\alpha_x}(\mathcal G^{\oplus m})_x$ is exact. Stalks commute with finite direct sums: the map $\sigma_n:(\mathcal G^{\oplus n})_x\to\mathcal G_x^{\oplus n}$, $((y_i)_i)_x\mapsto((y_i)_x)_i$, is a well-defined $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-linear bijection, by the description of germs in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]: it is well defined and linear because restriction in $\mathcal G^{\oplus n}$ is componentwise; surjective because $n$ germs $(y_i)_x$, $y_i\in\mathcal G(W_i)$, are represented by $y_i|_W$ on the open $W=\bigcap_iW_i\ni x$ (finite intersection; $W=X$ if $n=0$); injective because if every $(y_i)_x=0$ then $y_i|_{V_i}=0$ for opens $x\in V_i$, so $(y_i)_i$ vanishes on $\bigcap_iV_i$. In the same way $\sigma^{\mathcal O}_n:(\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n})_x\to\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\oplus n}$ is an isomorphism sending $(e_i)_x$ to the $i$-th standard basis vector $\bar e_i$. Under these identifications $\sigma_m\circ\alpha_x=\bar\alpha\circ\sigma_n$ with $\bar\alpha((z_i)_i)=(\sum_i(a_{ik})_xz_i)_k$, by the formula for $\alpha$ and $(ry)_x=r_xy_x$; and the induced $\bar a=\sigma^{\mathcal O}_n a_x(\sigma^{\mathcal O}_m)^{-1}:\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\oplus n}$ sends $\bar e_k\mapsto\sum_i(a_{ik})_x\bar e_i$. Hence $0\to\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal F,\mathcal G)_x\xrightarrow{\sigma_n\beta_x}\mathcal G_x^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\bar\alpha}\mathcal G_x^{\oplus m}$ is exact.

source.place: proof, third paragraph: 'Taking stalks we get an exact sequence 0 -> Hom(F,G)_x -> G_x^n -> G_x^m'

proof.text: *Step 5 (the free case on the stalk side).* Put $\bar b=b_x\circ(\sigma^{\mathcal O}_n)^{-1}:\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F_x$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact](5) to the exact sequence of Step 2 (exactness at $\mathcal O_X^{\oplus n}$ and at $\mathcal F$, the latter meaning $b_x$ surjective), $\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{\bar a}\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\bar b}\mathcal F_x\to0$ is an exact sequence of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-hom-left-exact](1) with $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $N=\mathcal G_x$, the sequence $0\to\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal F_x,\mathcal G_x)\xrightarrow{\bar b^*}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\oplus n},\mathcal G_x)\xrightarrow{\bar a^*}\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O_{X,x}^{\oplus m},\mathcal G_x)$ is exact, and by [lem-weil-pbc-module-hom-left-exact](2) the evaluations $\theta_n(\chi)=(\chi(\bar e_i))_i$, $\theta_m$ are bijections onto $\mathcal G_x^{\oplus n}$, $\mathcal G_x^{\oplus m}$ with $\theta_m\bar a^*=\bar\alpha\theta_n$ (since $\chi(\bar a(\bar e_k))=\sum_i(a_{ik})_x\chi(\bar e_i)$). So $\varepsilon=\theta_n\bar b^*:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_{X,x}}(\mathcal F_x,\mathcal G_x)\to\mathcal G_x^{\oplus n}$, $\varepsilon(\chi)=(\chi(\bar b(\bar e_i)))_i$, is injective with image $\operatorname{Ker}\bar\alpha$.

source.place: proof, third paragraph: 'the result follows since F_x sits in an exact sequence O_x^m -> O_x^n -> F_x -> 0 which induces the exact sequence 0 -> Hom(F_x,G_x) -> G_x^n -> G_x^m'

proof.text: *Step 6 (comparison; conclusion).* The triangle commutes: $\varepsilon\circ c=\sigma_n\circ\beta_x$. Indeed for a germ $(V,\psi)_x$, $\sigma_n\beta_x((V,\psi)_x)=(\psi_V(b_V(e_i|_V))_x)_i=(\psi_x(b_x((e_i)_x)))_i=(\psi_x(\bar b(\bar e_i)))_i=\varepsilon(\psi_x)$, using the formula for stalk maps of Step 1 and $(e_i)_x=(\sigma^{\mathcal O}_n)^{-1}(\bar e_i)$. By Steps 4 and 5, $\sigma_n\beta_x$ and $\varepsilon$ are both injective with the same image $\operatorname{Ker}\bar\alpha$. Hence $c$ is injective (as $\varepsilon c$ is) and surjective (for $\chi$, $\varepsilon(\chi)\in\operatorname{Ker}\bar\alpha$ equals $\sigma_n\beta_x(h)=\varepsilon(c(h))$ for some $h$, and $\varepsilon$ is injective, so $\chi=c(h)$). So $c$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$-modules (linear by Step 1).

lean.statement: theorem exists_stalk_internalHom_linearEquiv_of_finitePresentation (X : RingedSpace.{u}) (F G : SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj X.sheaf)) [SheafOfModules.IsFinitePresentation.{u} F] (x : X) : ∃ e : (moduleStalkFunctor X x).obj (F.homObj G) ≃ₗ[ X.presheaf.stalk x] ((moduleStalkFunctor X x).obj F →ₗ[X.presheaf.stalk x] (moduleStalkFunctor X x).obj G), ∀ (U : Opens X) (hxU : x ∈ U) (φ : (SheafOfModules.homObj F G).val.obj (op U)) (V : Opens X) (i : V ⟶ U) (hxV : x ∈ V) (s : F.val.obj (op V)), e (TopCat.Presheaf.germ (SheafOfModules.homObj F G).val.presheaf U x hxU φ) (TopCat.Presheaf.germ F.val.presheaf V x hxV s) = TopCat.Presheaf.germ G.val.presheaf V x hxV ((φ.app (op (Over.mk i))) s)
lean.note: The canonical map is specified by an explicit formula on representative germs; a linear equivalence with this formula states precisely its being an isomorphism.
